content:
DAAD scholarships are a collection of schemes with different purposes and eligibility rules. Choose the relevant scheme first, then check its academic requirements, application route and coverage.

What DAAD money actually is in 2026

DAAD's standard monthly rates are €992 for students and €1,300 for doctoral candidates, with postdoctoral rates higher. The payment is only part of the package: DAAD scholarships typically add payments toward health, accident and personal liability insurance, a travel allowance, and — for research grants — a study and research subsidy. Special schemes differ: the RISE Germany summer internship pays the same €992 monthly rate for a three-month research stay plus a €160 travel stipend for the closing meeting, and the one-year research-grant detail page lists €1,400 for specific calls, which is why reading the individual scholarship announcement matters more than memorising any table.

Deadlines cluster by scheme: annual research grants usually close between August and October for stays beginning the following northern autumn, RISE runs mid-October to early December for the next summer, and development-related postgraduate courses have their own windows. Coordinate the scholarship application with your admission timeline so an award letter can still be used for the visa.

[[chart:daad-rates]][[chart:daad-vs-cost]]

Building a DAAD application that clears the screen

DAAD screens on three axes: academic record, project quality and motivation fit. The academic axis wants transcripts plus a grading-scale explanation, because a CGPA without its scale is unreadable to a German reviewer. The project axis wants a research plan with a German host's involvement — for research grants, a supervisor's letter from a German institution is close to mandatory, and you secure it by emailing potential hosts with a specific proposal, not a CV. The motivation axis wants the German connection to be structural: why this scheme, why this host, why now — in that order.

Timeline discipline decides more outcomes than prose does. References in Germany are read literally and late ones kill applications, so brief your referees six weeks out with the form, the criteria and one paragraph on which of your work they should attest. Host invitations take three to eight weeks to arrange, so start that email campaign two months before the deadline. And keep the whole file consistent: the project title, the host, the dates and the budget must match across every form DAAD sees.

Choose the relevant scholarship scheme

Search the DAAD scholarship database using your academic level, country and subject. Read the individual announcement in full. Some schemes support a complete degree; others fund research visits or other activities. Requirements and application routes can differ considerably.

Check eligibility and coverage

Confirm academic qualifications, relevant experience where required, language evidence and the permitted timing of your previous degree. Read the listed funding period and allowances, then check whether tuition or other charges remain your responsibility. Avoid assuming one scheme provides the same benefits as another.

Coordinate the applications

A scholarship application and university admission may require separate submissions. Record both deadlines, identify the correct recipient for each document and allow time for references. Use the scheme announcement as the final checklist and ask the named contact about a specific ambiguity before submitting.

Read one scholarship announcement in full

Before collecting documents, identify the scheme that matches your academic level and purpose. Note the eligible countries, degree timing, language evidence and professional experience requirements where relevant. Write down whether applications go to DAAD, the university or another body. Check benefits separately rather than assuming the word “scholarship” covers every cost. If the announcement leaves an important detail unclear, contact the named office with a precise question. Keep its answer beside the scheme instructions, and check whether you also need a separate admission application.

Match the scheme to the work you want to do

There is no single DAAD application covering every international applicant. Begin by deciding whether you want a taught degree, a complete doctorate, a short research stay or another funded activity. Then filter the official database for your academic status and country. Two results with similar names can have different deadlines, eligibility conditions and application routes. Open the full announcement rather than relying on a search-result summary.

Read the selection criteria before drafting a motivation letter. An award focused on a particular discipline, professional background or research activity needs evidence relevant to that purpose. A general statement about wanting to study in Germany does not explain why that scheme should fund your proposed work. Make a short note against each criterion identifying the qualification, project or experience you can actually document.

Separate the funding decision from admission

DecisionEvidence to checkQuestion to resolve
Scholarship eligibilityFull scheme announcement and applicant guidanceDoes the scheme accept your nationality, degree stage and proposed activity?
Academic admissionUniversity or programme requirementsMust you obtain an offer or supervisor confirmation separately?
Financial coverageBenefits, duration and exclusionsWhich costs remain payable by you, and when do payments begin?
Submission routeOfficial application instructionsDoes the application go to DAAD, a university or another named body?

A useful working document has two columns: actions for admission and actions for funding. Put the exact deadline beside each one. If the scholarship requires a university document that is not yet available, check what the announcement permits. Do not upload an unrelated document just to fill a required field, and do not assume a deadline extension will be granted.

Build an application around one coherent plan

For a research award, explain the question you want to investigate, why the host is suitable, the methods you would use and what can reasonably be completed during the funded period. Label proposed work as proposed. A host's expertise can support feasibility, but do not imply access to a laboratory, dataset or supervisor until it has been confirmed.

For a taught programme, connect your previous preparation to actual course content. Name a relevant module or training component only after checking that it belongs to the intended intake. Explain the skills you need next and how the programme addresses that need. Avoid repeating your entire CV: the application should make the connection between experience, study choice and the scheme's purpose clear.

Give referees the correct announcement and an honest summary of your work. Tell them how their reference must be submitted and allow time for questions. Before submitting, compare dates, qualification names and project descriptions across the form, CV and statement. Small inconsistencies can be corrected without making the application sound more impressive than the evidence supports.

After submission and before accepting

Keep the submitted application and confirmation. Respond through the official channel if additional evidence is requested. If you receive an award, read the conditions as carefully as you read the benefits: check the start date, funding period, any reporting or renewal steps and conditions concerning other income. A scholarship should be assessed against the costs of the actual programme, not against the assumption that every DAAD award covers every expense.

Can I use one application for several DAAD schemes?

Reuse accurate background material where permitted, but check each scheme independently. Its documents, eligibility rules and purpose can differ. Submit through the route stated in the relevant announcement.

Does a scholarship automatically pay tuition?

Do not assume that it does. Read the named scheme's benefits and the university fee page together. Record any tuition or compulsory charge that remains outside the award before deciding whether the place is affordable.

Check the host arrangement before describing it

If the scheme needs a host or supervisor, establish what form of confirmation is required. A general conversation about research does not necessarily provide the document named in the announcement. Share a concise proposed plan and ask the host what they can confirm about supervision, dates and resources. Keep any unconfirmed access conditional in the application. This is particularly relevant to research visits, where a short funded period can be difficult to use well if data access or laboratory arrangements are still unresolved. Follow the announcement's document instructions rather than assuming an informal email is always sufficient.

Questions applicants often ask

How much is the DAAD scholarship per month in 2026?

€992 a month for students and €1,300 for doctoral candidates, plus insurance contributions, travel allowance and research subsidies depending on the scheme. Some special one-year research grants list €1,400.

Is a DAAD scholarship enough to live in Germany?

For students, €992 matches the blocked-account release and works outside the priciest cities; doctoral candidates at €1,300 live comfortably in most university cities. Munich and other expensive enclaves need savings or subsidised housing on top.
